title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Solicitation Assembly - Evaluation Criteria
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When drafting an RFP, the evaluation criteria and their respective weights must be established and finalized:
options: Immediately after proposals are opened but before they are read
Before the solicitation is publicly published and distributed to potential proposers
During the first meeting of the evaluation committee
After all vendor questions have been answered and the bid closes
questions.explain: To ensure fairness, transparency, and prevent manipulation of the scoring to favor a specific vendor, evaluation criteria and their weights must be firmly established prior to publishing the RFP.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency issues an RFP that lists 'Experience,' 'Technical Approach,' and 'Cost' as evaluation criteria, but fails to state their relative importance. How must vendors and evaluators legally interpret this under standard public procurement practices?
options: Cost is always worth 50% by default
All listed criteria must be assumed to carry equal weight
The evaluation committee can assign weights as they see fit during scoring
The RFP is immediately voided and cannot be corrected via addendum
questions.explain: If an RFP fails to declare the relative weighting or importance of the evaluation criteria, standard legal and ethical practice generally requires them to be treated as having equal importance.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'Mandatory' requirement in an evaluation matrix?
options: A requirement that is evaluated on a sliding scale from 1 to 10 points
A requirement that provides a small preference bonus to local businesses
A pass/fail condition that, if not met, results in immediate rejection of the proposal as non-responsive
An item that vendors can optionally choose to price separately
questions.explain: Mandatory requirements (e.g., minimum years in business, possession of a specific license) are evaluated strictly on a pass/fail basis. Failure to meet them means the proposal cannot be further evaluated.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A standard best practice for scoring the 'Cost/Price' criteria in an RFP evaluation matrix is to:
options: Assign it the lowest possible weight to focus on quality
Have the committee vote on whose price seems most fair
Use an objective mathematical formula where the lowest responsive price automatically receives the maximum allotted points for cost
Eliminate the highest and lowest prices and score only the median price
questions.explain: Unlike qualitative factors, cost should be scored using an objective mathematical formula. The lowest price typically receives 100% of the possible cost points, with higher prices receiving a proportionally lower score.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Many jurisdictions incorporate Local Preference policies into their IFBs or RFPs. What is the standard purpose of these policies?
options: To entirely exclude out-of-state vendors from submitting bids
To apply a specific percentage discount to a local vendor's bid price for evaluation purposes to encourage local economic development
To ensure local vendors do not have to pay performance bonds
To waive all insurance requirements for vendors located within the city limits
questions.explain: Local preference laws generally provide a competitive advantage to businesses located within the jurisdiction's boundaries by applying a mathematical discount or point bonus during evaluation, aiming to recirculate tax dollars locally.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Before access to RFP proposals is granted, what crucial document must every member of an evaluation committee sign to preserve the integrity of the procurement?
options: A Notice of Intent to Award
A Non-Disclosure and Conflict of Interest Declaration form
A Cooperative Purchasing Agreement
A Surety Bond
questions.explain: Evaluators must certify that they do not have personal, financial, or relational conflicts of interest with any of the proposing vendors, and they must agree to keep proposal contents confidential during the evaluation process.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following would be considered a highly subjective evaluation criterion in an RFP?
options: Total life-cycle cost of the equipment
The vendor possesses ISO 9001 certification
The creativity and visual appeal of the proposed marketing campaign
Number of similar projects completed in the last five years
questions.explain: Creativity and visual appeal are subjective because they rely on the personal judgment, tastes, and opinions of the evaluators, unlike quantifiable metrics like certifications or costs.
